For a 50-person Indian company, the purchase-ready shortlist is:

Option	Cost / commercial terms	Cancellation / refund	Support	Best fit
Yatra for Business	Quote-based. Travel Pro covers companies with <2,500 trips or <₹5 crore annual travel spend. 
Yatra.com
	Corporate fares can include free rescheduling, but fare difference applies. Refund follows airline policy. 
Yatra.com
	24/7 platform; support model depends on plan	Best for a typical 50-person Indian SME wanting simple implementation + flights/hotels/rail/cabs
FCM Travel India	Quote-based TMC fee + travel spend	Supplier/FCM cancellation fees can apply; supplier penalties can reach 100%. Refund waits for supplier funds. 
FCM Travel
	24/7 emergency assistance, travel policy, safety, visa and expense support. 
FCM Travel
	Better suited to higher-volume / international travel
Amex + TMC	Quote-based; Amex BTA centralises air spend rather than replacing the TMC	Airline/TMC rules apply	24/7 Global Assist; BTA includes up to ₹30 lakh business-travel accident insurance, subject to terms. 
American Express
	Finance-heavy companies wanting central billing + reconciliation
What I'd ask for before signing

Don't accept a generic quote. Get these in writing:

₹ booking fee for domestic air, international air, hotels and cancellations.

Any annual/minimum-spend commitment.

Exact refund SLA after airline/supplier releases funds.

Whether free rescheduling includes the TMC fee or only airline penalties.

24/7 human support and escalation SLA.

Credit terms and GST treatment.

Dedicated account manager.

Implementation/integration fees.

Whether unused tickets/credits remain fully traceable.

A sample monthly MIS + GST reconciliation report.

For a 50-person company, I'd take Yatra's Travel Pro quote as the baseline and make FCM match the same transaction-fee and SLA structure. The deciding number should be total annual TMC fees + avoidable cancellation/reissue costs, not the advertised fare discount.
